notes: All contexts used synthetic data and local mocked APIs; every nonlocal request was blocked. No real account, credential entry, OAuth flow, or upstream service was exercised.
The timeout case advanced the browser clock151000ms to exercise the real150000ms request timer and AbortController. This is not a measured service latency.

Initial integrated activity/health/CSV groups preceded the final authorization/disconnect and first-health error fixes. The directly affected final paths were tested separately; each report records its available run-start source hashes. The final production gate used built UI only.

The one explicit COROS save assertion creates exactly one synthetic source-bound activity inside an isolated test context. Other reads, guide previews, failures and navigation preserve fixture records/profile.
The former lap-selector harness timeout was corrected for its busy accessible name before the passing activity report. It was not an application failure.

Two earlier production attempts reached zero assertions because served HTML referenced missing old hashed JS/CSS. The mismatch was resolved by root with a clean build and preview restart. Their archived reports remain as resolved failure history and are excluded from the final count; the final nine-check built-UI gate passed against the current HTTP entry script.

Browser coverage for other watch brands verifies their existing guide/CSV preview boundary. Parser and import benchmarking are in the separate read-only data audit; no new online account integrations were invented.

resolvedProductionFailure.reason: Old entry HTML referenced missing hashed JS/CSS; clean build and preview restart restored matching assets.

benchmark.type: synthetic in-memory 20ms delay per upstream call

contract.authentication_failure: HTTP401 plus cleared cookies, no success data
contract.rate_limit: stop queued tools; retain completed values; explicitly list deferred tools in existing issues array

limitations: Measurements are synthetic; no real COROS or Garmin service was called.
Upstream request deadline remains25s; no overall server deadline added.
Separate HTTP requests have independent MCP sessions; no cross-request token cache was introduced.

client_proof.kind: COROS client targeted synthetic before/after verification
client_proof.network: All fetch responses are controlled stubs; zero external requests or real accounts
red_first_observed_failures: Original three simultaneous status readers issued three requests instead of one
Original two simultaneous health readers issued two requests instead of one
Successful health cache write emitted zero update events instead of one
Status read started before pending disconnect settled
Disconnect left linked metadata true and allowed old-session data reads
Delayed connected=true status fulfilled after a newer activity TOKEN_EXPIRED
Athlete switch released shared-cookie disconnect barrier and allowed an old-cookie status read
verified_guards: Owner mismatch rejects before health fetch
Athlete switch aborts old reads and blocks old-owner commit/return
Explicit authorization invalidation rejects old work without clearing imported records
Cookie-wide revocation barrier survives athlete changes while UI context generation advances
Data reads during and after successful disconnect reject TOKEN_EXPIRED without a fetch; status waits and reads fresh
TOKEN_EXPIRED blocks delayed status/data results without incrementing context generation
Ordinary network, malformed-body, rate-limit and timeout failures release pending work for manual retry
Older fetchedAt health rejects STALE_DATA without overwriting or returning the older data
Quota failure preserves stored cache and emits no successful-write event
HRV, stress, recovery, activity and lap fractional values remain exact; missing values and source identities are retained

integration_api.disconnect: corosMcpDisconnect() invalidates synchronously; callers capture their completion context after invocation

limits: No real-service timing measured; request-count improvement is deterministic synthetic evidence
Full application typecheck, production build and browser integration are owned by the root agent
Generic file parser remains unchanged in this client assignment

independent_auth_review.isolation: Node-only mocked fetch and storage. No actual credentials, services, user data, or application source edits.

checks.name: an older connected status cannot undo a newer authorization failure, including a subsequent status read
disconnect blocks new same-scope status, activity, and lap requests before revocation settles
the logout barrier survives an athlete switch, and the aborted prior health response cannot write either athlete
after logout, only fresh status is read; queued data reads reject without collection or cache writes
the review scenarios leave training/profile and health stores untouched

fractional activity/lap values and null-versus-zero semantics
health-trend previous/next/today navigation and existing charts
existing Garmin optimization source files byte-identical to baseline
no embedded personal plan or imported personal dataset
